# Data: Common Data Set

The Common Data Set is published by individual colleges and universities. Walker et al. use the "First-Time, First-Year Admissions" section, which reports applicant counts by sex.

For each institution-year, collect:

- institution name
- state
- academic year
- number of female applicants
- number of male applicants
- U.S. News rank used for sample selection
- percent out-of-state applicants, if you want to reproduce subgroup analyses
- URL or file path for the CDS source

## Raw data template

Create `data-raw/walker_cds_applicants.csv` with these columns:

```text
institution,state,year,female_applicants,male_applicants,us_news_rank,pct_out_state,source_url
```

The included toy file `data/example_cds_applicants.csv` has the same structure. It exists only so you can practice the code before the real collection is complete.

## Source discipline

The Walker paper also mentions IPEDS as a way to find CDS information when available. IPEDS describes itself as a source for information on U.S. colleges, universities, technical, and vocational institutions, and its site links to tools for downloading data submitted to NCES [@ipeds_home].

For a student replication, do not rely on "I found it somewhere online." Each row should have a source URL or local PDF path.

## Data checks

After collection:

```{r}
#| eval: false
source("R/functions.R")
panel <- prepare_applicant_panel()

panel |>
  dplyr::count(institution)

panel |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    min_year = min(year),
    max_year = max(year),
    missing_share = sum(is.na(share_female))
  )
```
